modern: All that comes from the gods is full of providence. What comes from fortune is not separate from nature, nor without being interwoven and entwined with the things which are ordered by providence. From there all things flow; and besides, there is necessity, and what is for the good of the whole universe, of which you are a part. But whatever the nature of the whole brings, and whatever serves to maintain this nature, is good for every part of nature. Now the universe is preserved, as by the changes of the elements, so by the changes of things made up of the elements. Let these principles be enough for you; let them always be fixed opinions. But throw away the thirst for books, so that you may not die grumbling, but cheerfully, truly, and thankful to the gods from your heart.
original: All that is from the gods is full of providence. That which is from fortune is not separated from nature or without an interweaving and involution with the things which are ordered by providence. From thence all things flow; and there is besides necessity, and that which is for the advantage of the whole universe, of which thou art a part. But that is good for every part of nature which the nature of the whole brings, and what serves to maintain this nature. Now the universe is preserved, as by the changes of the elements so by the changes of things compounded of the elements. Let these principles be enough for thee; let them always be fixed opinions. But cast away the thirst after books, that thou mayest not die murmuring, but cheerfully, truly, and from thy heart thankful to the gods.
